title: Control-plane API and rollback adapter for batching & caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a control-plane API surface and rollback adapter that lets Optimize recommend batching/caching config changes and safely apply or revert them. This ticket covers the backend endpoints, webhook event emission and validation, idempotency semantics, dry-run/preflight simulation and the SDK helpers required for safe, auditable automation of cost optimizations. The goal is to enable automated recommendations to be applied programmatically while ensuring deterministic rollback, clear audit trails, and low blast radius for production workloads.
background: We already generate batching and caching suggestions in Optimize. To turn recommendations into actionable system changes we need a server-side API and SDK primitives that support idempotent applies, robust rollback semantics, and webhook notifications to downstream systems (console, customers' orchestration). Prior attempts used ad-hoc scripts and manual steps which caused two incidents related to config drift and one failed rollback due to no preflight validation.
goals: Provide POST /v1/optimize/actions/apply endpoint with idempotency and dry-run
Provide POST /v1/optimize/actions/rollback endpoint that reverts applied recommendation operations
Ship SDK helper functions (Node/Python) to generate idempotency keys and run preflight validations
Record auditable entries (who/when/why) and link to operator traces and PRs
non_goals: Implement UI surfaces in Console (separate PM ticket)
Automated tuning of kernel selection as part of apply (out of scope)
Large-scale batch rollout orchestration (will rely on Dedicated autoscaling APIs)
api_contract_examples:
POST /v1/optimize/actions/apply
Request JSON fields: {
  "operation_id": "uuid-v4",
  "idempotency_key": "client-generated-hex",
  "recommendation_id": "rec-2026-0001",
  "actor": { "type": "service", "id": "auto-optimize" },
  "dry_run": true|false,
  "validate_only": true|false,
  "rollback_on_failure": true|false,
  "metadata": { "source": "weekly-scan" }
}
Responses: 202 Accepted (queued) with operation resource URL, 200 OK (applied synchronously), 409 Conflict (stale precondition), 400/422 Validation errors
Idempotency: server stores idempotency_key + operation_id mapping for 7 days; duplicate requests return existing operation result
idempotency_and_conflict_policy: Idempotency is client-driven via idempotency_key. The control-plane will also assign a canonical operation_id (uuid) for each unique apply. Applies check preconditions: recommendation version, model_variant compatibility, and current effective config hash. On mismatch the API returns 409 with current_effective_hash and a link to preflight simulation. Retried requests with same idempotency_key return the original operation result. Clients are encouraged to include an actor and correlation_id for traceability.
preflight_and_simulation: Apply endpoint supports dry_run and validate_only flags. Preflight runs the same validation pipeline as real apply but writes no state; returns a simulation bundle that includes: cost_estimate_delta, expected latency impact, KV-cache hit rate delta, and potential rollback actions. The response includes suggested rollback operation payload for fast revert.
rollback_behavior: Rollback requests accept operation_id or recommendation_id plus target_timestamp. Rollback attempts to replay the inverse of the applied delta and will fail fast if dependent changes have happened since the original apply (returns 409). On successful rollback we emit recommendation.lifecycle.rolled_back and create an audit entry linking the original apply and rollback operations.
sdk_helpers: Add high-level helpers in node and python sdks: applyRecommendation(recommendationId, {dryRun, idempotencyKey, validateOnly, rollbackOnFailure}) which returns an Operation object with poll(), wait(), and cancel(). Provide an IdempotencyKey.gen() utility that embeds timestamp+client-id and returns URL-safe base64 string. SDKs will auto-retry idempotency-related 429s with backoff and surface operation status changes via events.
observability_and_audit: Every API call must create an immutable audit record with fields: operation_id, idempotency_key, caller, request_payload, outcome, trace_id, and stack links. Console will show per-operation token-level cost delta and timeline. Instrument traces and metrics: optimize.apply.latency, optimize.rollback.latency, optimize.apply.success_rate, optimize.webhook.delivery_rate.
security_considerations: Require service tokens for automated agents; apply endpoints must require 'optimize.apply' scope and rollback requires 'optimize.rollback'. Webhooks signed with HMAC; include replay protection using timestamp and event_id. Security review required before release (see security_review_required). Avoid exposing raw model keys in audit logs; redact sensitive fields in stored payloads.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint /v1/optimize/actions/apply accepts idempotency_key and returns consistent results on repeated requests with same key
Dry-run (validate_only) returns simulation bundle with cost and latency deltas
Rollback endpoint reverts applied recommendations and emits signed webhook event
Webhook events signed and retried with exponential backoff; failed deliveries recorded to internal DLQ
SDKs include helpers for idempotency key generation and Operation.poll/wait semantics
Audit entries created for every apply/rollback with trace links and persisted for 90 days
Integration tests covering conflict 409 semantics, preflight mismatches, and successful rollback
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store, integration tests that run apply->simulate->apply->rollback in a staging environment, e2e test with SDK that validates event emission and DLQ behavior. Load test to ensure apply endpoint can handle bursts up to 200 RPS with 95th percentile latency under 300ms for simulation-only requests.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in staging -> 5% traffic in production with feature flag optimize.controlplane.apply -> monitor operation success rate and webhook delivery for 24h -> 50% -> 100%. Automatic rollback of the feature flag if failed_apply_rate > 2% for 1h.
open_questions: How long should idempotency keys be retained for long-running operations? (current proposal 7 days)
Should we allow cross-account rollback if actor is admin? (security implications)
Granularity of simulation bundle: full diff vs high-level deltas? Users asked for both in feedback
